contentBody: **Which statement best describes a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?**
option.1: The smallest offer that still delivers the core job and can be tested
option.2: A cheap unfinished app whose only purpose is to look broken on purpose
option.3: A logo plus a long site that looks like a company but tests nothing
option.4: Every feature from the later vision, shipped before anyone can try the job
answerExplanation: An MVP is the least you can show that still does one job and can be put in front of people. Looks, a broken toy, or the full vision are not that test.

contentBody: **What belongs on an early MVP include list?**
option.1: Payments, maps, ratings, and login so it already looks like a full product
option.2: Dark mode and a custom logo, even if they do not change what you learn
option.3: Only the pieces that help you learn about the core job in this version
option.4: Anything a simulated comment mentioned, including extras it invented
answerExplanation: If a piece does not help you learn about the core job this week, it stays off the include list. Polish and invented extras are excludes.

option.1: Rebuilding the whole site because a simulated user asked for a larger product
option.2: A small bounded change from evidence, then a recheck of the same questions
option.3: Changing the colours first, then deciding later whether the offer got clearer
option.4: Adding every requested feature so that nothing has to be parked for later
answerExplanation: Iteration is a bounded change from a finding, then a check. Rebuilding, decorating first, or shipping every request is not iteration.

contentBody: **After you change the page from a finding, what should you do next?**
option.1: Celebrate if an earlier simulation once said the old page was already perfect
option.2: Start a new product line so the old questions no longer have to apply at all
option.3: Hide the edit and skip checking whether the earlier stall on the page is gone
option.4: Re-run the same test questions on the new page text, and judge only that text
answerExplanation: After an edit, ask the same questions of the new text. If you cannot say what you will re-test, you are decorating.

contentBody: **A change blocks understanding or the next step, fits the MVP, and is quick. Where does it go?**
option.1: Later, because all clarity work is treated as decoration and should wait
option.2: Ignore, because only invented comments are allowed onto the Now list
option.3: Now: fix it in this sitting so learning about the core job can continue
option.4: Next: only a real user may ever be shown a clearer heading or button
answerExplanation: Now is for blockers of understanding or the call-to-action that fit the MVP and can be done in this sitting. Clarity beats extra features when time is short.
